setup: This is a question about interval notation.

steps.say: Interval notation says two things at once: which numbers are included, and how far the set runs. A square bracket means the endpoint is included, a round one means it is left out, and infinity always takes round brackets because it is never actually reached.
Here the lower endpoint is included and the upper one is not, so the left bracket is square and the right is round.
Here the set runs without limit to the right, so the right side is written as infinity, which always takes a round bracket.
Here the set runs without limit to the left, so the left side is written as minus infinity, again with a round bracket.
Neither endpoint is included, so both brackets are round.
